limit_order_match_in_progress.meaning: a limit order matching (partial or full) is being processed in _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder
limit_order_match_in_progress.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

matched_base_amount.meaning: matched base amount for the limit order match
matched_base_amount.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

matched_quote_amount.meaning: matched quote amount for the limit order match
matched_quote_amount.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

matched_base_is_power_of_two.meaning: the matched base amount is a power-of-two value 2^k
matched_base_is_power_of_two.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

matched_quote_less_than_base.meaning: the matched quote amount is less than the matched base amount 2^k
matched_quote_less_than_base.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

amounts_disjoint_bits.meaning: the two matched amounts have no overlapping 1-bits (bitwise AND is zero)
amounts_disjoint_bits.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade check during limit order matching

limit_order_matching_reverts.meaning: the limit order matching (partial or full) reverts instead of completing
limit_order_matching_reverts.checkpoint: during limit order matching after the zero-cost trade check

assumptions: The matched base and quote amounts are observable quantities at the checkpoint before the zero-cost trade check.
The report's power-of-two and disjoint-bit conditions are qualitative facts represented by grounded Boolean observables.

unresolved.description: Report does not state a common unit or scaling constant relating the matched base and quote amounts, so the 'quote less than base' comparison is represented as a report-grounded Boolean rather than a numeric comparison.
Report gives only examples (base = 256, quote in 1..255; 40 & 21 = 0) and no general numeric definition of the power-of-two or disjoint-bit conditions.

limitations: The impact text describes scope (all limit order matching, partial and full) rather than an explicit revert wording; the revert outcome is encoded as the negation of successful completion per the progress_or_liveness template.
Fill orders are stated to be unaffected; this claim covers only limit order matching.
